raw: `SqlExpr.tsx:81` — crashes the editor when `refIds` is empty (regression).

claim: Backtick-quoted table names are emitted into the Monaco buffer but nothing on the read-back path unquotes them: the mysql Monarch tokenizer splits `gdp per capita` into three tokens, the completion provider supplies no tables.parseName so defaultTableNameParser yields table='`', and fetchSQLFields in metaSqlExpr.ts:15 re-quotes (double-quoting a full quoted name yields a vitess parse error) while metaSqlExpr.ts:20's refId === query.table filter can never match; the failure is swallowed by catch { return [] } at sqlCompletionProvider.ts:39. Fix: unquoteIdentifier(query.table) before the re-quote and comparison, and add an IdentifierQuote-aware parseName. Rated Important only because column autocomplete is behind the experimental sqlExpressionsColumnAutoComplete flag.
raw: `sqlCompletionProvider.ts:27` + `metaSqlExpr.ts:15,20` — quoting the table name breaks column autocomplete for exactly the names this PR fixes.

claim: SqlExpr.tsx:13 and sqlCompletionProvider.ts:9 import the mysql quoteIdentifierIfNecessary (valid-name check plus ~250 reserved words), but metaSqlExpr.ts:15 resolves to a local copy at metaSqlExpr.ts:114-116 with no reserved-word check, so a refId like Order/Range/Key/System is quoted in the initial query and completion text but left bare in the metadata query (SELECT * FROM Order LIMIT 1 — a syntax error, silently swallowed). The two call sites must agree; pick one implementation.
raw: Two divergent `quoteIdentifierIfNecessary` implementations are now in play.

claim: In the second test all assertions sit inside `if (resolveFunc) { … }` with no expect(resolveFunc).toBeDefined() guard (unlike the first test at :14-29), so if provider.tables ever stops being populated the test passes having verified nothing. It also only checks `name`, never `completion`, so it does not exercise the changed line at all. Assert unconditionally, e.g. `const resolve = provider.tables!.resolve;`.
raw: `sqlCompletionProvider.test.ts:42-46` — the second test can pass without asserting anything.

claim: The third argument to the asserted call is queries.filter((q) => q.refId === query.table) — the very filter that the quoting round-trip issue breaks — but expect.anything() matches [] and so passes whether or not the refId lookup succeeded. Assert [{ refId: 'table with spaces' }] explicitly.

SqlExpr.tsx:13 and sqlCompletionProvider.ts:9 import app/plugins/datasource/mysql/sqlUtil; mysql is its own Yarn workspace (@grafana-plugins/mysql, package.json:479-485) listed in decoupled-plugins-overrides (eslint.config.js:463), and these are the only such core→plugin imports in public/app/features or packages/. Lint does not catch it (import/no-restricted-paths guards plugin→core only), but it couples core to a plugin being extracted and pulls the mysql RESERVED_WORDS table into the core bundle; export a single reserved-word-aware helper from the expressions module or @grafana/sql instead.
raw: Core feature code now imports from a decoupled plugin workspace.

claim: quoteIdentifierIfNecessary('a`b') returns `a`b` (backticks inside the identifier are not doubled), which vitess rejects; refIds are free-form so this is reachable, though it was equally broken before (not a regression) and is not a security issue since the query goes through /api/ds/query subject to parser_allow.go. Correct behavior is value.replace(/`/g, '``') before wrapping.
raw: Backticks inside identifiers are not escaped.
